quizzes.topic: Rest, Motion and Types of Motion

questions.q: Kinematics is the study of motion:
questions.explanation: Kinematics describes motion without concerning the forces that cause or change it.

questions.q: An object is said to be at rest if it:
options: does not change its position with respect to an observer with the passage of time
questions.explanation: Rest means no change in position with respect to the observer as time passes.

questions.q: A passenger sitting in a moving bus is:
options: at rest with respect to the road
in motion with respect to the bus
at rest with respect to the bus but in motion with respect to the road
questions.explanation: Rest and motion are relative; they depend on the observer (reference point).

questions.q: If all points of a moving object move uniformly in the same direction with no change in orientation, the motion is:
questions.explanation: This is the book's definition of translatory (translational) motion.

questions.q: The motion of the blades of a ceiling fan is:
questions.explanation: The blades rotate about a fixed axis, so the motion is rotatory.

questions.q: The to-and-fro motion of a swing or a plucked sitar string about its mean position is:
questions.explanation: Back-and-forth motion about a mean position is vibratory motion.

questions.q: The motion of a train on a straight track is:
questions.explanation: Translatory motion along a straight-line path is rectilinear motion.

questions.q: The motion of a car taking a turn is an example of:
questions.explanation: Translatory motion along a curved path is curvilinear motion.

questions.q: The motion of a butterfly or of clouds is:
questions.explanation: Translatory motion with no specific path is random motion.

questions.q: Circular motion is a special case of curvilinear motion in which:
options: the object moves in a straight line
the radius of the path remains constant
questions.explanation: In circular motion the object moves along a circle of constant radius.

questions.q: Translatory motion is divided into:
questions.explanation: The book divides translatory motion into rectilinear, curvilinear (incl. circular) and random motion.

questions.q: The Earth spinning on its axis shows ______ motion.
questions.explanation: Spinning about its own axis is rotatory motion.

questions.q: The length of path travelled between two positions is called:
questions.explanation: Distance is the total path length; it is a scalar.

questions.q: The shortest directed distance from initial position to final position is called:
questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight directed distance; it is a vector.

questions.q: Distance is a ______ quantity and displacement is a ______ quantity.
questions.explanation: Distance has no direction; displacement has direction.

questions.q: The SI unit of displacement is:
questions.explanation: Displacement is a length, so its SI unit is metre.

questions.q: Mathematically, displacement Δd is:
questions.explanation: Δd = final position − initial position = d₂ − d₁.

questions.q: An athlete completes one round of a 400 m circular track and stops at the starting point. His displacement is:
questions.explanation: Initial and final positions are the same, so displacement is zero (distance = 400 m).

questions.q: A girl walks 3 km east and then 4 km north. Her displacement is:
questions.explanation: √(3² + 4²) = 5 km, while the distance is 7 km.

questions.q: Distance and magnitude of displacement are equal when a body moves:
options: in a straight line in one direction
questions.explanation: Only for straight-line motion without turning back are the two equal.

questions.q: Which statement is always true?
questions.explanation: The straight path is the shortest, so displacement can never exceed distance.

questions.q: A boy walks 50 m to a shop and comes back along the same road. His distance and displacement are:
questions.explanation: Path length = 50 + 50 = 100 m; he returns to start, so displacement = 0.

questions.q: The Greek letter Δ (delta) in Δt represents:
questions.explanation: Δ means 'change in', e.g. Δt = t₂ − t₁.

quizzes.topic: Speed: Average, Instantaneous, Uniform and Variable

questions.q: Speed is defined as:
options: change in velocity per unit time
questions.explanation: v = distance ÷ elapsed time; it tells how fast an object moves.

questions.q: The SI unit of speed is:
questions.explanation: Speed = metre ÷ second = m s⁻¹.

questions.q: A car covers 70 km from Tarnol to Swabi interchange in 1 hour. Its speed is:
questions.explanation: v = 70 km ÷ 1 h = 70 km/h.

questions.q: Average speed is:
questions.explanation: v_ave = s ÷ t, averaging the increases and decreases in speed.

questions.q: The speedometer of a car shows:
questions.explanation: It shows the speed at that particular instant of time.

questions.q: If an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, it has:
questions.explanation: Equal distances in equal times = uniform speed.

questions.q: A Maglev train travels 30 km in 7 min 30 s. Its speed is about:
A ball bowled at 44.8 m/s travels 17.5 m to the batsman. The time taken is about:
36 km/h is equal to:
The universal speed limit for any object in the universe is approximately:
questions.explanation: Nothing with mass can reach the speed of light, about 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.q: The speed of sound in air is roughly:
questions.explanation: Sound travels at about 343 m/s in air — far slower than light.

questions.q: Speed is a scalar quantity because it:
questions.explanation: Speed does not specify direction.

quizzes.topic: Velocity: Average, Instantaneous, Uniform and Variable

questions.q: Velocity is defined as:
options: change in speed per unit time
questions.explanation: v = Δd ÷ Δt; it has the direction of displacement.

questions.q: Velocity is a vector quantity whose direction is the same as that of:
questions.explanation: Velocity has the same direction as the displacement vector.

questions.q: Average velocity is:
questions.explanation: v_ave = total displacement ÷ total time.

questions.q: A body covers equal displacements in equal intervals of time. Its velocity is:
questions.explanation: Equal displacements in equal times (same speed and direction) = uniform velocity.

questions.q: A satellite moving with constant speed in a circular orbit has:
questions.explanation: Its direction changes continuously, so its velocity is variable.

questions.q: Velocity of a body can change by changing its:
questions.explanation: Velocity changes if speed, direction or both change.

questions.q: A car runs 800 m on a curved track in 40 s, while the straight-line distance between start and end is 600 m. Its average velocity is:
questions.explanation: v_ave = 600 m ÷ 40 s = 15 m/s (average speed = 800 ÷ 40 = 20 m/s).

questions.q: A horse moves 60 m right in 3 s, then turns back and moves 30 m in 2 s. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ time = 90 m ÷ 5 s = 18 m/s.

questions.q: For straight-line motion in one direction, speed and velocity have:
questions.explanation: Distance equals displacement there, so the magnitudes are equal.

questions.q: Velocity measured over a very small time interval is called:
questions.explanation: Velocity at a particular moment, with direction, is instantaneous velocity.

questions.q: A runner completes one full lap of a circular track in 50 s. His average velocity for the lap is:
questions.explanation: Displacement for a full lap is zero, so average velocity is zero.

questions.q: The time rate of change of velocity is called:
questions.explanation: a = Δv ÷ Δt = (v₂ − v₁) ÷ (t₂ − t₁).

questions.q: The SI unit of acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Metre per second per second = m s⁻².

questions.q: Acceleration is a vector quantity in the direction of:
questions.explanation: Acceleration has the same direction as Δv.

questions.q: Negative acceleration (deceleration) means that the velocity:
questions.explanation: Deceleration is a decrease in velocity with time.

questions.q: A body has uniform acceleration if:
options: equal changes in velocity occur in equal intervals of time
questions.explanation: Velocity changing at the same rate every second = uniform acceleration.

questions.q: When the rate of change of velocity is not the same throughout the motion, the acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Non-uniform acceleration occurs when the velocity change is not steady over time.

questions.q: A cheetah goes from rest to 26.8 m/s in 3 s. Its acceleration is about:
questions.explanation: a = (26.8 − 0) ÷ 3 ≈ 8.9 m/s² (typical cars: only 3–4 m/s²).

questions.q: A car moving at 20 m/s stops in 5 s. Its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: a = (0 − 20) ÷ 5 = −4 m/s²; the minus sign shows deceleration.

questions.q: A drone moving at constant speed changes its direction. It is:
questions.explanation: A change in direction alone changes velocity, so it accelerates.

questions.q: A car moving towards the east is slowing down. The direction of its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: During deceleration, acceleration is opposite to the motion.

questions.q: A bus moves with a constant velocity of 15 m/s on a straight road. Its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: No change in velocity means zero acceleration.

questions.q: A cyclist increases speed from 2 m/s to 8 m/s in 3 s. The acceleration is:
The acceleration of freely falling bodies is called:
questions.explanation: It is denoted by g.

questions.q: Near the Earth's surface, the value of g is approximately:
The acceleration due to gravity is directed:
options: downward towards the centre of the Earth
in the direction of motion always
questions.explanation: g always points towards the Earth's centre.

questions.q: The scientist who dropped objects of different masses from the Leaning Tower of Pisa was:
questions.explanation: Galileo found they all reach the ground at the same time.

questions.q: In the absence of air resistance, a heavy stone and a light stone dropped together will:
questions.explanation: All freely falling bodies have the same acceleration, independent of mass.

questions.q: In air, a coin falls faster than a sheet of paper because of:
questions.explanation: Air resistance slows the paper more; in vacuum both fall together.

questions.q: For a body thrown vertically upward, g is taken as:
questions.explanation: Moving against gravity, g is taken as negative.

questions.q: A ball is dropped from rest. Its speed after 3 s is (g = 9.8 m/s²):
A block dropped from a building strikes the ground at 78.5 m/s. The time of fall is about:
questions.explanation: t = v ÷ g = 78.5 ÷ 9.8 ≈ 8 s (book Example 2.5).

questions.q: A ball thrown upward reaches its highest point in 2 s. Its initial speed was:
questions.explanation: Velocity drops by 9.8 m/s each second: v = 9.8 × 2 = 19.6 m/s.

questions.q: At the highest point of its path, a ball thrown upward has:
options: zero velocity but acceleration 9.8 m/s² downward
questions.explanation: It stops momentarily but gravity still acts on it.

questions.q: A freely falling body's velocity increases every second by about:
questions.explanation: g = 9.8 m/s² means velocity increases 9.8 m/s per second.

questions.q: In a distance-time graph, time is plotted along the:
questions.explanation: Time on x-axis, distance on y-axis.

questions.q: The gradient (slope) of a distance-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Gradient = Δs ÷ Δt = speed.

questions.q: A horizontal straight line on a distance-time graph shows that the body is:
questions.explanation: Distance does not change with time, so the body is at rest.

questions.q: A straight line sloping upward on a distance-time graph shows:
questions.explanation: Constant slope means constant (uniform) speed.

questions.q: A distance-time curve bending upward (slope increasing) shows:
questions.explanation: Increasing slope means the speed is increasing (accelerating).

questions.q: A distance-time curve bending downward (slope decreasing) shows:
questions.explanation: Decreasing slope means the body is slowing down.

questions.q: A distance-time graph always lies in the positive XY plane because:
questions.explanation: Distance never goes negative, irrespective of direction of motion.

questions.q: Two points on a distance-time line are (1 s, 10 m) and (4 s, 40 m). The speed is:
A car travels 100 km in the first hour (Peshawar to rest area). The gradient of this part of its graph is:
questions.explanation: Gradient = 100 km ÷ 1 h = 100 km/h (= 27.78 m/s).

questions.q: On a distance-time graph, a steeper straight line means:
questions.explanation: A steeper slope means more distance per unit time.

questions.q: A car covers 175 km in 2.5 h including a 30 min stop. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Average speed = 175 km ÷ 2.5 h = 70 km/h (stop time is included).

questions.q: The gradient of a speed-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Gradient = Δv ÷ Δt = acceleration.

questions.q: The area under a speed-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: E.g. rectangle area = v × t = distance.

questions.q: A horizontal line on a speed-time graph (above the time axis) shows:
questions.explanation: Speed does not change, so acceleration is zero.

questions.q: A straight line sloping upward from the origin on a speed-time graph shows:
questions.explanation: Speed increases at a constant rate.

questions.q: A straight line sloping downward on a speed-time graph shows:
questions.explanation: Speed decreases at a constant rate.

questions.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 30 m/s in 20 s. Its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Slope = 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5 m/s² (book Example 2.7).

questions.q: In the same example, the distance covered in those 20 s is:
questions.explanation: Area of triangle = ½ × 30 × 20 = 300 m.

questions.q: A car moves at a constant 30 m/s for 30 s. Distance covered is:
questions.explanation: Area of rectangle = 30 × 30 = 900 m.

questions.q: A car slows uniformly from 30 m/s to rest in 10 s. Its deceleration is:
For a body starting from rest with uniform acceleration reaching speed v in time t, the distance from the graph is:
questions.explanation: The area under the graph is a triangle: ½ × v × t.

questions.q: A car moves at 20 m/s for 20 s and then stops uniformly in 30 s. Total distance is:
questions.explanation: Rectangle 20 × 20 = 400 m + triangle ½ × 20 × 30 = 300 m = 700 m.

questions.q: A body covers 1350 m in 60 s. Its average speed is:
Change in position of a body from initial to final point is called:
questions.explanation: Displacement is the change in position (d₂ − d₁).

questions.q: Motion of a screw of rotating fan is:
questions.explanation: It spins about its own axis, so the motion is rotatory.

questions.q: A cyclist is travelling in a westward direction and produces a deceleration of 8 m/s² to stop. The direction of its acceleration is towards:
questions.explanation: Deceleration acts opposite to motion: west → east.

questions.q: A girl walks 3 km towards west and 4 km towards south. What is the magnitude of her total distance and displacement respectively?
questions.explanation: Distance = 3 + 4 = 7 km; displacement = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km.

questions.q: A rider is training a horse. Horse moves 60 metres towards right in 3 seconds. Then it turns back and travels 30 metres in 2 seconds. Find its average velocity?
questions.explanation: Displacement = 60 − 30 = 30 m; time = 5 s; v = 30 ÷ 5 = 6 m/s.

questions.q: If a cyclist has acceleration of 2 m/s² for 5 seconds, the change in velocity of the cyclist is:
A car is moving with velocity of 10 m/s. If it has acceleration of 2 m/s² for 10 seconds, what is final velocity of the car?
When the slope of a body's displacement-time graph increases, the body is moving with:
questions.explanation: Slope of displacement-time graph = velocity; increasing slope means increasing velocity.

questions.q: A ball is thrown straight up, what is the magnitude of acceleration at the top of its path?
questions.explanation: Velocity is zero at the top, but g = 9.8 m/s² still acts.

questions.q: Slope of distance-time graph is:
questions.explanation: Δs ÷ Δt = speed (distance is scalar, so speed, not velocity).

questions.q: Area under speed-time graph is equal to ______ of moving body:
questions.explanation: Area = speed × time = distance.

questions.q: In 5 s a car accelerates so that its velocity increases by 20 m/s. The acceleration is:
Ball dropped freely from a tower reaches ground in 4 s, the speed of impact of ball is:
Which of the following distance-time graphs represents increasing speed of a car?
questions.explanation: Increasing slope of distance-time graph means increasing speed.
